Hi Sofia,

Quick question as we're finishing our DPA review with legal/security: can you confirm whether we can require all Mediconnect production traffic to be processed in the EU region (specific: Frankfurt/Amsterdam) under your hosted offering?

Our security team is also asking about fallback behaviour — if a primary EU pool is unavailable, will requests route to non-EU capacity by default (and what legal mechanism backs that behaviour)? We need to understand whether SCCs + the UK IDTA (when in-scope) are sufficient, or whether we should ask for a binding clause in the DPA that prevents non-EU failover for production tenant data.

Also: do you publish a subprocessor map that shows which regions your cloud infra providers may route through (eg. transient egress via us-east1)? If you can attach a recent map and a short note on the operational fallback/resiliency design that would be great.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Security Programs
Mediconnect

--
P.S. I can escalate to procurement if there is a straightforward amendment path.

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear set of asks, and great to hear you're close on DPA review. Short answers up front:

- Yes, we can pin Mediconnect production to the EU region for served requests and caching/KV residency.
- Fallback: our standard runtime supports tiered fallbacks (EU -> dedicated EU spare capacity -> region-compatible model variants). We do not automatically fail to non-EU by default for pinned production tenants unless there is an explicit capacity emergency and the customer has agreed to a "cross-region fallback" clause.

I attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (current template with a marked section for regional processing), subprocessor_map_aug2026.csv, and a small routing-diagram.png that illustrates typical failover paths.

Longer note below on legal mechanisms and recommended amendment. I'm looping in Kimberly to confirm implementation constraints and Jonas for TIA/UK IDTA alignment.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai

----
Longer explanation:
1) Legal: We rely on SCCs (EU standard contractual clauses) for controller-processor transfers and our DPA template includes a UK IDTA addendum for UK customers. Where customers require a guarantee that non-EU fallback never occurs, we propose an amendment that explicitly disallows cross-border fallback except under a declared "disaster emergency" that must be escalated to your security and legal contacts. That amendment is reasonably simple to add to the DPA.

2) Technical/Operational: We maintain region pins for routing and a per-tenant preference. In normal autoscale/maintenance scenarios requests remain in-region. Fallback to other regions is a controlled action (automated only if a capacity policy permits and the customer opted into burst/fallback).

3) Subprocessor visibility: the attached CSV lists infra partners and potential transient regions. Our policy is to avoid non-EU compute for EU-pinned tenants unless fallback is allowed.

Action items: I suggest we 1) propose a narrow DPA amendment clause for "no non-EU fallback without mutual consent"; 2) have a short technical note from Kimberly confirming how often transient egress occurs for control-plane operations; 3) share DocuSign for the amendment if Mediconnect wants to proceed.

Sofia — quick ops confirmation for the thread.

- Transient control-plane traffic: we occasionally route logs/metrics to our analytics stack which runs in multi-region; those control-plane flows do not contain raw customer prompts, and are pseudonymized. We document this in the subprocessor map under "observability providers".
- Data-plane processing (model inference): for EU-pinned tenants we run compute in EU and keep KV caches in-region. We only promote cross-region inference if the tenant's policy explicitly allows "emergency cross-region failover" or if the tenant is on a Dedicated plan with configured cross-region burst.
- In a declared disaster emergency we have an internal playbook that notifies both the customer SRE and legal lead prior to any cross-border promotion; uptake is on a case-by-case basis.

I'll draft a short ops blurb that can be added as an exhibit to the DPA (3–4 bullets). Jonas — can you confirm any outstanding TIA/DTIA evidence we should include?

Thanks,

Putting TIA perspective in this thread. For Mediconnect (health data footprint) we should include:

- A short TIA summary confirming processing locations and legal mechanism (SCCs/UK IDTA).
- A sampling approach for periodic DTIA attestations — propose quarterly routing-scan reports (hash-matched traces) for the first 6 months post-onboard, then quarterly thereafter.
- An acceptance criteria sheet for any cross-border fallback request (must include incident severity threshold, expected duration, and explicit written concurrence from the customer's security contact).

I'll attach a TIA checklist we can include as an annex. If Mediconnect wants stronger contractual guarantees (complete ban on non-EU processing even in disaster), that'll require an expanded SLA and potentially Dedicated capacity — I can scope latency/availability tradeoffs for that.
